arXiv:2109.06058v1 [math.AP] 31 Aug 2021

Asymptotic behavior of solutions toward the rarefaction waves to the Cauchy problem for the generalized Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation with dissipative term

Natsumi Yoshida Email: 14v00067@gmail.com Address:  Address: Graduate Faculty of Interdisciplinary Research Faculty of Education, University of Yamanashi, Kofu, Yamanashi 400-8510, Japan.
Abstract

In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of solutions to the Cauchy problem with the far field condisiton for the generalized Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation with a fourth-order dissipative term. When the corresponding Riemann problem for the hyperbolic part admits a Riemann solution which consists of single rarefaction wave, it is proved that the solution of the Cauchy problem tends toward the rarefaction wave as time goes to infinity. We can further obtain the same global asymptotic stability of the rarefaction wave to the generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation with a fourth-order dissipative term as the former one.

Keywords: 
Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation , Korteweg-de Vries-Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation , convex flux , asymptotic behavior , rarefaction wave AMS subject classifications: 35K55, 35B40, 35L65

1 Introduction and main theorems

In this paper, we consider the asymptotic behavior of solutions to the Cauchy problem for the generalized Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation with a fourth-order dissipative term

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u))−α​∂t∂x2u−β​∂x2u+γ​∂x4u=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞).\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\big(\,f(u)\,\big)-\alpha\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}u-\beta\,\partial_{x}^{2}u+\gamma\,\partial_{x}^{4}u=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty).\end{array}\right.\,

Here, u=u⁡(t,x)u=u(t,x) is the unknown function of t>0t>0 and x∈ℝx\in\mathbb{R}, and α\alpha, β\beta, γ\gamma are positive constants u0u_{0} is the initial data, and u±∈ℝu_{\pm}\in\mathbb{R} are the prescribed far field states. We suppose that ff is a smooth function.

There are many results concerning with the mathematical structure, such as the global existence and time-decay properties of solutions, of the generalized Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation with the dissipative terms (see Kondo-Webler [21], [22], [23], [24], Wang [49], Xu-Li [51] Zhao-Xuan [64] and so on). The model (1.1) is closely related to the following Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation

∂tu+δ​∂xu+u​∂xu−α​∂t∂x2u−β​∂x2u=0,\partial_{t}u+\delta\,\partial_{x}u+u\,\partial_{x}u-\alpha\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}u-\beta\,\partial_{x}^{2}u=0, (1.4)

where δ∈ℝ\delta\in\mathbb{R}. The mathematical structure of (1.2) have also been investigated by Amick-Bona-Schonbek [1], Mei [37], [38], Mei-Schmeiser [39], Naumkin [40] and so on. When β=0\beta=0, then (1.2) becomes the following Benjamin-Bona-Mahony equation

∂tu+δ​∂xu+u​∂xu−α​∂t∂x2u=0,\partial_{t}u+\delta\,\partial_{x}u+u\,\partial_{x}u-\alpha\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}u=0, (1.5)

which was advocated by [3] as a refinement of the following Korteweg de-Vries equation

∂tu+δ​∂xu+u​∂xu−α​∂x3u=0.\partial_{t}u+\delta\,\partial_{x}u+u\,\partial_{x}u-\alpha\,\partial_{x}^{3}u=0. (1.6)

For the case α=1\alpha=1 and β=0\beta=0 of (1.2), (1.2) is the so-called regularized long wave equation, which was proposed by Peregrine [44] and [3], as follows.

∂tu+δ​∂xu+u​∂xu−∂t∂x2u=0.\partial_{t}u+\delta\,\partial_{x}u+u\,\partial_{x}u-\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}u=0. (1.7)

We note that (1.3) and (1.5) are known as the approximated models for the long waves of small amplitude.

We are going to obtain the rarefaction stability of the solution to (1.1). Therefore we deal with the case where the flux function ff is fully convex, that is,

f′′​(u)>0(u∈ℝ),f^{\prime\prime}(u)>0\quad(u\in\mathbb{R}), (1.8)

and u−<u+u_{-}<u_{+}. Then, since the corresponding Riemann problem (cf. [27])

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u))=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0R​(x):={u−(x<0),u+(x>0)\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\bigl(\,f(u)\,\bigr)=0\,\>\;\qquad\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}^{\rm{R}}(x):=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}u_{-}&\;(x<0),\\[5.0pt] u_{+}&\;(x>0)\end{array}\right.\end{array}\right.\,

turns out to admit a single rarefaction wave solution, we expect that the solution of the Cauchy problem (1.1) tends toward the rarefaction wave as time goes to infinity. Here, the rarefaction wave connecting u−u_{-} to u+u_{+} is given by

ur​(xt,u−,u+)={u−(x≤f′​(u−)​t),(f′)−1​(xt)(f′​(u−)​t≤x≤f′​(u+)​t),u+(x≥f′​(u+)​t).u^{r}\left(\,\frac{x}{t}\>;\>u_{-},\>u_{+}\right)=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}u_{-}&\;\bigl(\,x\leq f^{\prime}(u_{-})\,t\,\bigr),\\[7.0pt] \displaystyle{(f^{\prime})^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{t}\right)}&\;\bigl(\,f^{\prime}(u_{-})\,t\leq x\leq f^{\prime}(u_{+})\,t\,\bigr),\\[7.0pt] u_{+}&\;\bigl(\,x\geq f^{\prime}(u_{+})\,t\,\bigr).\end{array}\right. (1.14)

In particular, we also expect that if u−=u+=:u~u_{-}=u_{+}=:\tilde{u}, then the solution of the Cauchy problem (1.1) tends toward the constant state u~\tilde{u} as time goes to infinity.

There are many results conserning with the rarefaction stabilities. For viscous conservation law,

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u)−μ​∂xu)=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\bigl(\,f(u)-\mu\,\partial_{x}u\,\bigr)=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

with the condition (1.6), Il’in-Oleĭnik [18] showed that the solution tends toward the single rarefaction wave under the condition u−<u+u_{-}<u_{+} (and the one does the single viscous shock wave under the condition u−>u+u_{-}>u_{+}, for further studies, see [34], [35], [53], [61] and so on). Hattori-Nishihara [16] also obtained the pointwise and time-decay estimates of the difference |u−ur||\,u-u^{r}\,|. Harabetian [14] further considered the following rarefaction problem for a quasilinear parabolic equation

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u)−A′​(u)​∂xu)=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\bigl(\,f(u)-A^{\prime}(u)\,\partial_{x}u\,\bigr)=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

where A′​(u)≥0A^{\prime}(u)\geq 0 (u∈ℝ)(u\in\mathbb{R}), and obtained the precise time-decay estimates of global stability of the rarefaction wave with the aid of the arguments on monotone semigroups by Osher-Ralston [42]. For the following Cauchy problem of the Matsumura-Nishihara model

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u)−μ​|∂xu|p−1​∂xu)=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\bigl(\,f(u)-\mu\,|\,\partial_{x}u\,|^{p-1}\,\partial_{x}u\,\bigr)=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

where p>1p>1 and the viscosity μ​|∂xu|p−1​∂xu\mu\,|\,\partial_{x}u\,|^{p-1}\,\partial_{x}u is the so-called Ostwald-de Waele-type viscosity advocated by de Waele [9] and Ostwald [43] (which is a typical example for the non-Newtonian viscosity, see also [6], [7], [8], [19], [25], [30], [31], [48] and so on), Matsumura-Nishihara [33] first investigated and proved the global stability of the rarefaction wave by using the technical energy method. Yoshida [54] further obtained its precise time-decay estimates by using the time-weighted energy method (for the stabilities of the multiwave pattern, see [55], [56], [57]). Furthermore, Matsumura-Yoshida [36] considered the following Cauchy problem of the non-Newtonian viscous conservation law

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u)−σ⁡(∂xu))=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\Big(\,f(u)-\sigma\big(\,\partial_{x}u\,\big)\,\Big)=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

where viscosity function σ\sigma satisfies the conditions

{σ(0)=0,σ′(v)>0(v∈ℝ),|σ(v)|∼|v|p,|σ′(v)|∼|v|p−1(|v|→∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\sigma(0)=0,\quad\sigma^{\prime}(v)>0\quad(v\in\mathbb{R}),\\[5.0pt] |\,\sigma(v)\,|\sim|\,v\,|^{p},\quad|\,\sigma^{\prime}(v)\,|\sim|\,v\,|^{p-1}\quad\big(\,|\,v\,|\rightarrow\infty\,\big),\end{array}\right.\,

and obtained the global stability of the rarefaction wave for the case 0<p<3/70<p<3/7. Recently, Yoshida [60] obtained this rarefaction stability for more general case 0<p<1/30<p<1/3 and its precise time-decay estimates. For the rarefaction problem of the Korteweg-de Vries equation

{∂tu+∂x(−3​u2+∂x2u)=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)​{→0(x→∞),→u−>0(x→−∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\bigl(\,-3\,u^{2}+\partial_{x}^{2}u\,\bigr)=0\qquad\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\rightarrow 0&(x\rightarrow\infty),\\[5.0pt] \rightarrow u_{-}>0&(x\rightarrow-\infty),\end{array}\right.\end{array}\right.\,

Egorova-Grunert-Teschl [12] and Egorova-Teschl [13] obtained the existence and uniqueness in some class of the classical solution , and Andreiev-Egorova-Lange-Teschl [2] also obtained the valid asymptotic formula of the solution. For diffusive dispersive conservation laws, Wang-Zhu [50] obtained the local stability of the rarefaction wave for the following Cauchy problem of the generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u)−μ​∂xu+δ​∂x2u)=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞).\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\bigl(\,f(u)-\mu\,\partial_{x}u+\delta\,\partial_{x}^{2}u\,\bigr)=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty).\end{array}\right.\,

Duan-Zhao [11] and Yoshida [59] further obtained the global stabilities of the rarefaction wave under some growth conditions for ff (for stability and time-decay properties of a travelling wave, see [4], [5], [41]). For the Cauchy problem of the generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers-Kuramoto equation

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u)−μ​∂xu+δ​∂x2u+ν​∂x3u)=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\bigl(\,f(u)-\mu\,\partial_{x}u+\delta\,\partial_{x}^{2}u+\nu\,\partial_{x}^{3}u\,\bigr)=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

Ruan-Gao-Chen [47] first obtained the local stability of the rarefaction wave. Duan-Fan-Kim-Xie [10] and Yoshida [59] also obtained the global stability of the rarefaction wave under some growth conditions for ff. Recently, Yoshida [63] (see also [62]) investigated the following Cauchy problem for a diffusive dispersive conservation waw, that is, the generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers-Kuramoto equation without the viscosity term as

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u)+δ​∂x2u+ν​∂x3u)=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\bigl(\,f(u)+\delta\,\partial_{x}^{2}u+\nu\,\partial_{x}^{3}u\,\bigr)=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

and obtained the global stability of the rarefaction wave under some growth conditions for ff.

Our main results of the present paper are as follows.

Theorem 1.1 (Main Theorem I). Assume the far field states u±u_{\pm} satisfy u−=u+=u~u_{-}=u_{+}=\tilde{u}, and the convective flux f∈C2​(ℝ)f\in C^{2}(\mathbb{R}). Further assume the initial data satisfy u0−u~∈L2u_{0}-\tilde{u}\in L^{2} and ∂xu0∈H2\partial_{x}u_{0}\in H^{2}. Then the Cauchy problem (1.1) has a unique global in time solution uu satisfying

{u−u~∈C0​([ 0,∞),H3),∂xu∈L2​( 0,∞,H3),∂tu∈L2​( 0,∞,H2),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}u-\tilde{u}\in C^{0}\bigl(\,[\,0,\,\infty\,)\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{x}u\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{t}u\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{2}\,\bigr),\end{array}\right.\,

and the asymptotic behavior

limt→∞(supx∈ℝ|u⁡(t,x)−u~|+supx∈ℝ|∂xu⁡(t,x)|+supx∈ℝ|∂x2u⁡(t,x)|)=0.\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigg(\,\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,u(t,x)-\tilde{u}\,|+\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\partial_{x}u(t,x)\,|+\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\partial_{x}^{2}u(t,x)\,|\,\bigg)=0.

Theorem 1.2 (Main Theorem II). Assume the far field states u±u_{\pm} satisfy u−<u+u_{-}<u_{+}, and the convective flux f∈C5​(ℝ)f\in C^{5}(\mathbb{R}) satisfy (1.6). Further assume the initial data satisfy u0−u0R∈L2u_{0}-u_{0}^{\rm{R}}\in L^{2} and ∂xu0∈H2\partial_{x}u_{0}\in H^{2}. Then the Cauchy problem (1.1) has a unique global in time solution uu satisfying

{u−u0R∈C0​([ 0,∞),H3),∂xu∈Lloc2​( 0,∞,H3),∂tu∈Lloc2​( 0,∞,H2),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}u-u_{0}^{\rm{R}}\in C^{0}\bigl(\,[\,0,\,\infty\,)\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{x}u\in L^{2}_{\rm{loc}}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{t}u\in L^{2}_{\rm{loc}}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{2}\,\bigr),\end{array}\right.\,

and the asymptotic behavior

{limt→∞supx∈ℝ|u⁡(t,x)−ur​(xt,u−,u+)|=0,limt→∞supx∈ℝ|∂xu⁡(t,x)−∂xur​(t,x,u−,u+)|=0,limt→∞supx∈ℝ|∂x2u⁡(t,x)−∂x2ur​(t,x,u−,u+)|=0,\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle{\lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\,\left|\,u(t,x)-u^{r}\left(\,\frac{x}{t}\>;\>u_{-},\,u_{+}\,\right)\,\right|}=0,\\[10.0pt] \displaystyle{\lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\,|\,\partial_{x}u(t,x)-\partial_{x}u^{r}\left(\,t,\,x\>;\>u_{-},\,u_{+}\,\right)\,|}=0,\\[10.0pt] \displaystyle{\lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\,|\,\partial_{x}^{2}u(t,x)-\partial_{x}^{2}u^{r}\left(\,t,\,x\>;\>u_{-},\,u_{+}\,\right)\,|}=0,\end{array}\right.\,

where ∂xur\partial_{x}u^{r} and ∂x2ur\partial_{x}^{2}u^{r} are given by

∂xur​(t,x,u−,u+)={0(x≤f′​(u−)​t),1f′′​((f′)−1​(xt))​1t(f′​(u−)​t≤x≤f′​(u+)​t),0(x≥f′​(u+)​t),\partial_{x}u^{r}\left(\,t,\,x\>;\>u_{-},\,u_{+}\,\right)=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}0&\;\bigl(\,x\leq f^{\prime}(u_{-})\,t\,\bigr),\\[7.0pt] \displaystyle{\frac{1}{f^{\prime\prime}\bigg(\,(f^{\prime})^{-1}\left(\displaystyle{\frac{x}{t}}\right)\,\bigg)}\,\frac{1}{t}}&\;\bigl(\,f^{\prime}(u_{-})\,t\leq x\leq f^{\prime}(u_{+})\,t\,\bigr),\\[15.0pt] 0&\;\bigl(\,x\geq f^{\prime}(u_{+})\,t\,\bigr),\end{array}\right.
∂x2ur​(t,x,u−,u+)={0(x≤f′​(u−)​t),1(f′′​((f′)−1​(xt)))3​xt3−1f′′​((f′)−1​(xt))​1t2(f′​(u−)​t≤x≤f′​(u+)​t),0(x≥f′​(u+)​t).\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\partial_{x}^{2}u^{r}\left(\,t,\,x\>;\>u_{-},\,u_{+}\,\right)\\ &=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}0&\;\bigl(\,x\leq f^{\prime}(u_{-})\,t\,\bigr),\\[7.0pt] \displaystyle{\frac{1}{\left(\,f^{\prime\prime}\bigg(\,(f^{\prime})^{-1}\left(\displaystyle{\frac{x}{t}}\right)\,\bigg)\,\right)^{3}}\,\frac{x}{t^{3}}-\frac{1}{f^{\prime\prime}\bigg(\,(f^{\prime})^{-1}\left(\displaystyle{\frac{x}{t}}\right)\,\bigg)}\,\frac{1}{t^{2}}}&\;\bigl(\,f^{\prime}(u_{-})\,t\leq x\leq f^{\prime}(u_{+})\,t\,\bigr),\\[15.0pt] 0&\;\bigl(\,x\geq f^{\prime}(u_{+})\,t\,\bigr).\end{array}\right.\end{aligned}

Furthermore, for the Cauchy problem for the generalized Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation with third-order dispersive and fourth-order dissipative terms, the so-called generalized Korteweg-de Vries-Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation with a fourth-order dissipative term (see [46])

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u))−α​∂t∂x2u−β​∂x2u+δ​∂x3u+γ​∂x4u=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\big(\,f(u)\,\big)-\alpha\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}u-\beta\,\partial_{x}^{2}u+\delta\,\partial_{x}^{3}u+\gamma\,\partial_{x}^{4}u=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

where δ∈ℝ\delta\in\mathbb{R}, we can obtain the same stabilities as Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 in the next theorems.

Theorem 1.3 (Main Theorem III). Assume the far field states u±u_{\pm} satisfy u−=u+=u~u_{-}=u_{+}=\tilde{u}, and the convective flux f∈C2​(ℝ)f\in C^{2}(\mathbb{R}). Further assume the initial data satisfy u0−u~∈L2u_{0}-\tilde{u}\in L^{2} and ∂xu0∈H2\partial_{x}u_{0}\in H^{2}. Then for the Cauchy problem (1.9), the same result as in Theorem 1.1 holds true.

Theorem 1.4 (Main Theorem IV). Assume the far field states u±u_{\pm} satisfy u−<u+u_{-}<u_{+}, and the convective flux f∈C5​(ℝ)f\in C^{5}(\mathbb{R}) satisfy (1.6). Further assume the initial data satisfy u0−u0R∈L2u_{0}-u_{0}^{\rm{R}}\in L^{2} and ∂xu0∈H2\partial_{x}u_{0}\in H^{2}. Then for the Cauchy problem (1.9), the same result as in Theorem 1.2 holds true.

We finally remark that when γ=δ=0\gamma=\delta=0, the problem (1.9) becomes the following Cauchy problem for usual generalized Benjamin-Bona-Mahony-Burgers equation.

{∂tu+∂x(f⁡(u))−α​∂t∂x2u−β​∂x2u=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),u⁡(0,x)=u0​(x)→u±(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}u+\partial_{x}\big(\,f(u)\,\big)-\alpha\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}u-\beta\,\partial_{x}^{2}u=0&\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[5.0pt] u(0,x)=u_{0}(x)\rightarrow u_{\pm}&(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

We can also obtain the similar stabilities as Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 in the next theorems.

Theorem 1.5. Assume the far field states u±u_{\pm} satisfy u−=u+=u~u_{-}=u_{+}=\tilde{u}, and the convective flux f∈C2​(ℝ)f\in C^{2}(\mathbb{R}). Further assume the initial data satisfy u0−u~∈L2u_{0}-\tilde{u}\in L^{2} and ∂xu0∈H2\partial_{x}u_{0}\in H^{2}. Then the Cauchy problem (1.10) has a unique global in time solution uu satisfying

{u−u~∈C0​([ 0,∞),H3),∂xu∈L2​( 0,∞,H2),∂tu∈L2​( 0,∞,H2),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}u-\tilde{u}\in C^{0}\bigl(\,[\,0,\,\infty\,)\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{x}u\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{2}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{t}u\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{2}\,\bigr),\end{array}\right.\,

and the asymptotic behavior

limt→∞(supx∈ℝ|u⁡(t,x)−u~|+supx∈ℝ|∂xu⁡(t,x)|+supx∈ℝ|∂x2u⁡(t,x)|)=0.\lim_{t\to\infty}\bigg(\,\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,u(t,x)-\tilde{u}\,|+\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\partial_{x}u(t,x)\,|+\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\partial_{x}^{2}u(t,x)\,|\,\bigg)=0.

Theorem 1.6. Assume the far field states u±u_{\pm} satisfy u−<u+u_{-}<u_{+}, and the convective flux f∈C5​(ℝ)f\in C^{5}(\mathbb{R}) satisfy (1.6). Further assume the initial data satisfy u0−u0R∈L2u_{0}-u_{0}^{\rm{R}}\in L^{2} and ∂xu0∈H2\partial_{x}u_{0}\in H^{2}. Then the Cauchy problem (1.10) has a unique global in time solution uu satisfying

{u−u0R∈C0​([ 0,∞),H3),∂xu∈Lloc2​( 0,∞,H2),∂tu∈Lloc2​( 0,∞,H2),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}u-u_{0}^{\rm{R}}\in C^{0}\bigl(\,[\,0,\,\infty\,)\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{x}u\in L^{2}_{\rm{loc}}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{2}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{t}u\in L^{2}_{\rm{loc}}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{2}\,\bigr),\end{array}\right.\,

and the asymptotic behavior

{limt→∞supx∈ℝ|u⁡(t,x)−ur​(xt,u−,u+)|=0,limt→∞supx∈ℝ|∂xu⁡(t,x)−∂xur​(t,x,u−,u+)|=0,limt→∞supx∈ℝ|∂x2u⁡(t,x)−∂x2ur​(t,x,u−,u+)|=0,\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\displaystyle{\lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\,\left|\,u(t,x)-u^{r}\left(\,\frac{x}{t}\>;\>u_{-},\,u_{+}\,\right)\,\right|}=0,\\[10.0pt] \displaystyle{\lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\,|\,\partial_{x}u(t,x)-\partial_{x}u^{r}\left(\,t,\,x\>;\>u_{-},\,u_{+}\,\right)\,|}=0,\\[10.0pt] \displaystyle{\lim_{t\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\,|\,\partial_{x}^{2}u(t,x)-\partial_{x}^{2}u^{r}\left(\,t,\,x\>;\>u_{-},\,u_{+}\,\right)\,|}=0,\end{array}\right.\,

where ∂xur\partial_{x}u^{r} and ∂x2ur\partial_{x}^{2}u^{r} are given in Theorem 1.2.

Because the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.3-1.6 are similarly given as or easier than that for Theorem 1.2, we only show Theorem 1.2 in the following sections.

This paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we construct the approximation of the rarefaction wave and prepare the basic properties of the rarefaction wave and the approximated one. We reformulate the problem in terms of the deviation from the asymptotic state in Section 3. In order to show the asymptotics, we establish the a priori estimates by using the technical energy method in Section 4. Finally in Section 5, we give several uniform estimates by using the a priori estimates in Sections 3 and 4.

Some Notation. We denote by CC generic positive constants unless they need to be distinguished. In particular, use Cα,β,⋯C_{\alpha,\beta,\cdots} when we emphasize the dependency on α,β,⋯\alpha,\>\beta,\>\cdots.

For function spaces, Lp=Lp​(ℝ){L}^{p}={L}^{p}(\mathbb{R}) and Hk=Hk​(ℝ){H}^{k}={H}^{k}(\mathbb{R}) denote the usual Lebesgue space and kk-th order Sobolev space on the whole space ℝ\mathbb{R} with norms ||⋅||Lp||\cdot||_{{L}^{p}} and ||⋅||Hk||\cdot||_{{H}^{k}}, respectively.

2 Preliminaries

In this section, we prepare the several lemmas concerning with the basic properties of the rarefaction wave for the proof of the main Theorem 1.2. Since the rarefaction wave uru^{r} is not smooth enough, we construct a smooth approximated one. To do that, we first consider the rarefaction wave solution wrw^{r} to the Riemann problem for the non-viscous Burgers equation

{∂tw+∂x(12​w2)=0(t>0,x∈ℝ),w⁡(0,x)=w0R​(x,w−,w+):={w+(x>0),w−(x<0),\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}\partial_{t}w+\displaystyle{\partial_{x}\left(\,\frac{1}{2}\,w^{2}\right)}=0\,\,\;\;\qquad\quad\qquad\big(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\big),\\[7.0pt] w(0,x)=w_{0}^{\rm{R}}(\,x\>;\>w_{-},\>w_{+}\,):=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}w_{+}&\,\>\;\quad(x>0),\\[5.0pt] w_{-}&\,\>\;\quad(x<0),\end{array}\right.\end{array}\right. (2.1)

where w±∈ℝ⁡(w−<w+)w_{\pm}\in\mathbb{R}\>(w_{-}<w_{+}) are the prescribed far field states. The unique global weak solution w=wr​(x/t,w−,w+)w=w^{r}\left(\,x/t\>;\>w_{-},\>w_{+}\,\right) of (2.1) is explicitly given by

ur​(xt,u−,u+)=(λ)−1​(wr​(xt,λ−,λ+))u^{r}\left(\,\frac{x}{t}\>;\>u_{-},\>u_{+}\,\right)=(\lambda)^{-1}\biggl(\,w^{r}\left(\,\frac{x}{t}\>;\>\lambda_{-},\>\lambda_{+}\,\right)\,\biggr) (2.3)

which is nothing but (1.6), where λ±:=λ⁡(u±)=f′​(u±)\lambda_{\pm}:=\lambda(u_{\pm})=f^{\prime}(u_{\pm}). We define a smooth approximation of wr​(xt,w−,w+)w^{r}(\,\frac{x}{t}\>;\>w_{-},\>w_{+}\,) by the unique classical solution

3 Reformulation of the problem

In this section, we reformulate our problem (1.1) in terms of the deviation from the asymptotic state. Putting ϕ\phi as

u⁡(t,x)=Ur​(t,x)+ϕ⁡(t,x),u(t,x)=U^{r}(t,x)+\phi(t,x), (3.1)

we reformulate the problem (1.1) in terms of the deviation ϕ\phi from UrU^{r} as

{∂tϕ+∂x(f⁡(ϕ+Ur)−f⁡(Ur))−α∂t∂x2ϕ−β∂x2ϕ+γ∂x4ϕ=F(Ur)(t>0,x∈ℝ),ϕ⁡(0,x)=ϕ0​(x):=u0​(x)−Ur​(0,x)→0(x→±∞),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}\phi+\partial_{x}\big(\,f(\phi+U^{r})-f(U^{r})\,\big)\\[5.0pt] \quad-\alpha\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi-\beta\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi+\gamma\,\partial_{x}^{4}\phi=F(U^{r})\quad\bigl(\,t>0,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \phi(0,x)=\phi_{0}(x):=u_{0}(x)-U^{r}(0,x)\rightarrow 0\quad(x\rightarrow\pm\infty),\end{array}\right.\,

where

F⁡(Ur):=α​∂t∂x2Ur+β​∂x2Ur−δ​∂x3Ur−γ​∂x4Ur.F(U^{r}):=\alpha\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}U^{r}+\beta\,\partial_{x}^{2}U^{r}-\delta\,\partial_{x}^{3}U^{r}-\gamma\,\partial_{x}^{4}U^{r}.

Then we look for the unique global in time solution ϕ\phi which has the asymptotic behavior

∑k=13supx∈ℝ|∂xkϕ⁡(t,x)|→0(t→∞).\displaystyle{\sum_{k=1}^{3}\,\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left|\,\partial_{x}^{k}\phi(t,x)\,\right|\to 0\qquad(t\to\infty)}. (3.6)

Here we note that ϕ0∈H3\phi_{0}\in H^{3} by the assumptions on u0u_{0} and Lemma 2.2. Then the corresponding theorems for ϕ\phi to Theorem 1.2 we should prove is as follows.

Theorem 3.1. (Global Existence). Assume the far field states u±u_{\pm} satisfy u−<u+u_{-}<u_{+}, and the convective flux f∈C5​(ℝ)f\in C^{5}(\mathbb{R}) satisfy (1.6). Further assume the initial data satisfy ϕ0∈H3\phi_{0}\in H^{3}. Then the Cauchy problem (3.2) has a unique global in time solution ϕ\phi satisfying

{ϕ∈C0​([ 0,∞),H3),∂xϕ∈L2​( 0,∞,H3),∂tϕ∈L2​( 0,∞,H2),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\phi\in C^{0}\bigl(\,[\,0,\,\infty)\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{x}\phi\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{t}\phi\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{2}\,\bigr),\end{array}\right.\,

and the asymptotic behavior

limt→∞∑k=02supx∈ℝ|∂xkϕ⁡(t,x)|=0.\lim_{t\to\infty}\,\sum_{k=0}^{2}\,\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\left|\,\partial_{x}^{k}\phi(t,x)\,\right|=0.

In order to obtain Theorem 3.1, we prepare the local existence precisely, we formulate the problem (3.2) at general initial time τ≥0\tau\geq 0:

{∂tϕ+∂x(f⁡(ϕ+Ur)−f⁡(Ur))−α∂t∂x2ϕ−β∂x2ϕ+γ∂x4ϕ=F(Ur)(t>τ,x∈ℝ),ϕ⁡(τ,x)=ϕτ​(x):=uτ​(x)−Ur​(τ,x)→0(x→±∞).\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\partial_{t}\phi+\partial_{x}\big(\,f(\phi+U^{r})-f(U^{r})\,\big)\\[5.0pt] \quad-\alpha\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi-\beta\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi+\gamma\,\partial_{x}^{4}\phi=F(U^{r})\quad\bigl(\,t>\tau,\>x\in\mathbb{R}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \phi(\tau,x)=\phi_{\tau}(x):=u_{\tau}(x)-U^{r}(\tau,x)\rightarrow 0\quad(x\rightarrow\pm\infty).\end{array}\right.\,

Theorem 3.2 (Local Existence). For any M>0M>0, there exists a positive constant t0=t0​(M)t_{0}=t_{0}(M) not depending on τ\tau such that if ϕτ∈H3\phi_{\tau}\in H^{3} and

‖ϕτ‖H3≤M,\displaystyle{\|\,\phi_{\tau}\,\|_{H^{3}}\leq M},

then the Cauchy problem (3.4) has a unique solution ϕ\phi on the time interval [τ,τ+t0​(M)][\,\tau,\,\tau+t_{0}(M)\,] satisfying

{ϕ∈C0​([τ,τ+t0],H3),∂xϕ∈L2​(τ,τ+t0,H3),∂tϕ∈L2​(τ,τ+t0,H2),supt∈[τ,τ+t0]‖ϕ⁡(t)‖H3≤2​M.\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\phi\in C^{0}\bigl(\,[\,\tau,\,\tau+t_{0}\,]\,;H^{3}\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{x}\phi\in L^{2}\bigl(\,\tau,\,\tau+t_{0}\,;H^{3}\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{t}\phi\in L^{2}\bigl(\,\tau,\,\tau+t_{0}\,;H^{2}\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \displaystyle{\sup_{t\in[\tau,\tau+t_{0}]}\,\|\,\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{3}}}\leq 2\,M.\end{array}\right.\,

Because the proof of Theorem 3.2 is standard, we omit the details here (cf. [52], [64]). The a priori estimates we establish in Section 4 are the following.

Theorem 3.3 (A Priori Estimates). Under the same assumptions as in Theorem 3.1, for any initial data ϕ0∈H3\phi_{0}\in H^{3}, there exists a positive constant Cϕ0C_{\phi_{0}} such that if the Cauchy problem (3.1) has a solution ϕ\phi on the time interval [ 0,T][\,0,\,T\,] satisfying

{ϕ∈C0​([ 0,T],H3),∂xϕ∈L2​( 0,T,H3),∂tϕ∈L2​( 0,T,H2),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\phi\in C^{0}\bigl(\,[\,0,\,T\,]\,;H^{3}\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{x}\phi\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,T\,;H^{3}\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{t}\phi\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,T\,;H^{2}\bigr),\end{array}\right.\,

for some positive constant TT, then it holds that

‖ϕ⁡(t)‖H32+∫0t‖(∂xUr​ϕ)​(τ)‖L22​𝑑τ+∫t0∥∂xϕ(τ)∥H32dτ+∫t0∥∂tϕ(τ)∥H22dτ≤Cϕ0(t∈[ 0,T]).\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\|\,\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{3}}^{2}+\int^{t}_{0}\big\|\,\big(\,\sqrt{\partial_{x}U^{r}}\>\phi\,\big)(\tau)\,\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}\tau\\ &+\int^{t}_{0}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(\tau)\,\|_{H^{3}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}\tau+\int^{t}_{0}\|\,\partial_{t}\phi(\tau)\,\|_{H^{2}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}\tau\leq C_{\phi_{0}}\quad\big(\,t\in[\,0,\,T\,]\,\big).\end{aligned} (3.14)

Combining the local existence Theorem 3.2 together with the a priori estimates, Theorem 3.3, we can obtain global existence Theorem 3.1. In fact, we can obtain the unique global in time solutions ϕ\phi to (3.2) in Theorem 3.1 satisfying

{ϕ∈C0​([ 0,∞),H3),∂xϕ∈L2​( 0,∞,H3),∂tϕ∈L2​( 0,∞,H2),\displaystyle\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}\phi\in C^{0}\bigl(\,[\,0,\,\infty)\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{x}\phi\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{3}\,\bigr),\\[5.0pt] \partial_{t}\phi\in L^{2}\bigl(\,0,\,\infty\,;H^{2}\,\bigr),\end{array}\right.\,

and

supt≥0‖ϕ⁡(t)‖H32+∫0∞‖(∂xUr​ϕ)​(t)‖L22​𝑑t+∫∞0∥∂xϕ(t)∥H32dt+∫∞0∥∂tϕ(t)∥H22dt<∞\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\sup_{t\geq 0}\|\,\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{3}}^{2}+\int^{\infty}_{0}\big\|\,\big(\,\sqrt{\partial_{x}U^{r}}\>\phi\,\big)(t)\,\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}t\\ &\quad+\int^{\infty}_{0}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{3}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}t+\int^{\infty}_{0}\|\,\partial_{t}\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{2}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}t<\infty\end{aligned} (3.16)

which yields

∫0∞|dd​t​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22|​𝑑t<∞,∫0∞|dd​t​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22|​𝑑t<∞.\int_{0}^{\infty}\bigg|\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}t<\infty,\quad\int_{0}^{\infty}\bigg|\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}t<\infty. (3.17)

In fact, by using (3.6), direct computation shows that

∫0∞|dd​t​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22|​𝑑t=2​∫0∞|∫−∞∞∂xϕ​∂t∂xϕ​𝑑x|​𝑑t≤∫0∞(‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22+‖∂t∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22)​dt<∞,\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \int_{0}^{\infty}\bigg|\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}t&=2\,\int_{0}^{\infty}\left|\,\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\partial_{x}\phi\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}\phi\,\mathrm{d}x\,\right|\,\mathrm{d}t\\ &\leq\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\right)\,\mathrm{d}t<\infty,\end{aligned} (3.18)
∫0∞|dd​t​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22|​𝑑t=2​∫0∞|∫−∞∞∂x2ϕ​∂t∂x2ϕ​𝑑x|​𝑑t≤∫0∞(‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22+‖∂t∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22)​dt<∞.\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \int_{0}^{\infty}\bigg|\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\bigg|\,\mathrm{d}t&=2\,\int_{0}^{\infty}\left|\,\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\mathrm{d}x\,\right|\,\mathrm{d}t\\ &\leq\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\right)\,\mathrm{d}t<\infty.\end{aligned} (3.19)

From (3.8) and (3.9), we get (3.7). We immediately have from (3.7) that

limt→∞‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L2=0,limt→∞‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L2=0.\lim_{t\to\infty}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}=0,\quad\lim_{t\to\infty}\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}=0. (3.20)

Further from (3.10), by using the Sobolev inequality, we obtain the desired asymptotic behavior (3.3) as follows.

supx∈ℝ|ϕ⁡(t,x)|≤2​‖ϕ⁡(t)‖L212​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L212→0(t→∞),\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\phi(t,x)\,|\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\rightarrow 0\quad\big(\,t\rightarrow\infty\,\big),
supx∈ℝ|∂xϕ⁡(t,x)|≤2​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L212​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L212→0(t→∞),\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t,x)\,|\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\rightarrow 0\quad\big(\,t\rightarrow\infty\,\big),
supx∈ℝ|∂x2ϕ⁡(t,x)|≤2​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L212​‖∂x3ϕ⁡(t)‖L212→0(t→∞).\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t,x)\,|\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{3}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\rightarrow 0\quad\big(\,t\rightarrow\infty\,\big).

Thus Theorems 3.1 is proved.

4 A priori estimates

In this section, we show the following a priori estimate for ϕ\phi in Theorem 3.3. To do that, we prepare the following basic estimate.

Proposition 4.1. There exists a positive constant Cϕ0C_{\phi_{0}} such that

‖ϕ⁡(t)‖H12+∫0t∫−∞∞∫0ϕ(f′​(η+Ur)−f′​(Ur))​𝑑η​∂xUr​𝑑x​𝑑τ+∫t0∥∂xϕ(τ)∥H12dτ≤Cϕ0(t∈[ 0,T]).\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\|\,\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\int^{t}_{0}\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\int^{\phi}_{0}\bigl(\,f^{\prime}(\eta+U^{r})-f^{\prime}(U^{r})\,\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\eta\,\partial_{x}U^{r}\,\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}\tau\\ &+\int^{t}_{0}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(\tau)\,\|_{H^{1}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}\tau\leq C_{\phi_{0}}\quad\big(\,t\in[\,0,\,T\,]\,\big).\end{aligned}

Proof of Proposition 4.1. Multiplying the equation in (3.2) by ϕ\phi and integrating it with respect to xx, we have, after integration by parts, that

12​dd​t​‖ϕ⁡(t)‖L22+α2​dd​t​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22+∫∞−∞∫ϕ0(f′(η+Ur)−f′(Ur))dη∂xUrdx+β​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22+γ​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22=∫−∞∞ϕ​F​(Ur)​dx.\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\frac{1}{2}\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\,\|\,\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\frac{\alpha}{2}\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\\ &+\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\int^{\phi}_{0}\bigl(\,f^{\prime}(\eta+U^{r})-f^{\prime}(U^{r})\,\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\eta\,\partial_{x}U^{r}\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &+\beta\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\gamma\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}=\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\phi\,F(U^{r})\,\mathrm{d}x.\end{aligned} (4.1)

By making use of the Sobolev inequality and the Young inequality, we estimate the right-hand-side of (4.1) as follows.

|∫−∞∞ϕ​F​(Ur)​dx|≤2​‖ϕ‖L212​‖∂xϕ‖L212​‖F⁡(Ur)‖L1≤β2​‖∂xϕ‖L22+Cβ​‖ϕ‖L223​‖F⁡(Ur)‖L143≤β2​‖∂xϕ‖L22+Cβ​( 1+‖ϕ‖L22)​‖F⁡(Ur)‖L143.\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \left|\,\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\phi\,F(U^{r})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\right|&\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\,\|\,F(U^{r})\,\|_{L^{1}}\\ &\leq\frac{\beta}{2}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+C_{\beta}\,\|\,\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{2}{3}}\,\|\,F(U^{r})\,\|_{L^{1}}^{\frac{4}{3}}\\ &\leq\frac{\beta}{2}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+C_{\beta}\,\left(\,1+\|\,\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\right)\,\|\,F(U^{r})\,\|_{L^{1}}^{\frac{4}{3}}.\end{aligned} (4.2)

Substituting (4.2) into (4.1), integrating the resultant inequality with respect to tt, noting

∂t∂xUr=−f′′​(Ur)​|∂xUr|2−f′​(Ur)​∂x2Ur,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}U^{r}=-f^{\prime\prime}(U^{r})\,|\,\partial_{x}U^{r}\,|^{2}-f^{\prime}(U^{r})\,\partial_{x}^{2}U^{r},
‖F⁡(Ur)‖L143≤Cα,u±​‖∂xUr‖L283+Cα,β,u±​‖∂x2Ur‖L143+γ43​‖∂x4Ur‖L143∈Lt1​(0,∞)\|\,F(U^{r})\,\|_{L^{1}}^{\frac{4}{3}}\leq C_{\alpha,u_{\pm}}\,\|\,\partial_{x}U^{r}\,\|_{L^{2}}^{\frac{8}{3}}+C_{\alpha,\beta,u_{\pm}}\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}U^{r}\,\|_{L^{1}}^{\frac{4}{3}}+\gamma^{\frac{4}{3}}\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{4}U^{r}\,\|_{L^{1}}^{\frac{4}{3}}\in L_{t}^{1}(0,\,\infty)

from Lemma 2.2, and using the Gronwall inequality, we obtain the desired estimate.

Thus, we complete the proof of Proposition 4.1.

Olny from Proposition 4.1, using the Sobolev inequality, we can easily get the uniform boundedness of ϕ\phi in the next lemma (cf. [17], [20], [26]).

Lemma 4.2. There exists a positive constant Cϕ0C_{\phi_{0}} such that

supt∈[0,T],x∈ℝ|ϕ⁡(t,x)|≤Cϕ0.\sup_{t\in[0,T],\,x\in\mathbb{R}}\,|\,\phi(t,x)\,|\leq C_{\phi_{0}}.

By the uniform boundedness of ϕ\phi, Lemma 4.2, we note that the second term on the left-hand side of the a priori estimate in Proposition 4.1 can be replaced by the left-hand side of the following inequality as

∫0t∫−∞∞∫0ϕ(f′​(η+Ur)−f′​(Ur))​𝑑η​∂xUr​𝑑x​𝑑τ≥Cϕ0−1​∫0t‖(∂xUr​ϕ)​(τ)‖L22​dτ.\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\int^{t}_{0}\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\int^{\phi}_{0}\bigl(\,f^{\prime}(\eta+U^{r})-f^{\prime}(U^{r})\,\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}\eta\,\partial_{x}U^{r}\,\mathrm{d}x\mathrm{d}\tau\\ &\geq C_{\phi_{0}}^{-1}\,\int^{t}_{0}\big\|\,\big(\,\sqrt{\partial_{x}U^{r}}\>\phi\,\big)(\tau)\,\big\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\mathrm{d}\tau.\end{aligned} (4.3)

We now prepare the following propieties for the a priori estimates for the derivatives of ϕ\phi in the next lemma.

Lemma 4.3. There exists a positive constant Cϕ0C_{\phi_{0}} such that

∫0t‖(f⁡(ϕ+Ur)−f⁡(Ur))​(τ)‖L22​𝑑τ≤Cϕ0(t∈[ 0,T]),\int_{0}^{t}\left\|\,\bigl(\,f(\phi+U^{r})-f(U^{r})\,\bigr)(\tau)\,\right\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}\tau\leq C_{\phi_{0}}\quad\big(\,t\in[\,0,\,T\,]\,\big),
∫0t‖F⁡(Ur)​(τ)‖L22​𝑑τ≤Cϕ0(t∈[ 0,T]).\int_{0}^{t}\left\|\,F(U^{r})(\tau)\,\right\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\mathrm{d}\tau\leq C_{\phi_{0}}\quad\big(\,t\in[\,0,\,T\,]\,\big).

Proof of Lemma 4.3. The second estimate, that is, the time-integrability of ‖F⁡(Ur)‖L22\left\|\,F(U^{r})\,\right\|_{L^{2}}^{2}, is obtained by Lemma 2.2. Noting Proposition 4.1 and using Lagrange’s mean-value theorem, we can also obtain the first estimate, that is, the time-integrability of ‖f⁡(ϕ+Ur)−f⁡(Ur)‖L22\left\|\,f(\phi+U^{r})-f(U^{r})\,\right\|_{L^{2}}^{2}.

Thus, the proof of Lemma 4.3 is completed.

Next, we show the a priori estimate for ∂xϕ\partial_{x}\phi and ∂x2ϕ\partial_{x}^{2}\phi as follows.

Proposition 4.4. There exists a positive constant Cϕ0C_{\phi_{0}} such that

‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖H12+∫0t(‖∂tϕ⁡(τ)‖H12+‖∂x2ϕ⁡(τ)‖H12)​𝑑τ≤Cϕ0(t∈[ 0,T]).\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\int^{t}_{0}\left(\,\|\,\partial_{t}\phi(\tau)\,\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(\tau)\,\|_{H^{1}}^{2}\,\right)\,\mathrm{d}\tau\leq C_{\phi_{0}}\quad\big(\,t\in[\,0,\,T\,]\,\big).

Proof of Proposition 4.4. Multiplying the equation in (3.2) by ∂tϕ−∂x2ϕ\partial_{t}\phi-\partial_{x}^{2}\phi and integrating it with respect to xx, we have, after integration by parts, that

β+12​dd​t​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22+γ+12​dd​t​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22+‖∂tϕ⁡(t)‖L22+α​‖∂t∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22+β​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22+γ​‖∂x3ϕ⁡(t)‖L22=−∫∞−∞(∂tϕ−∂x2ϕ)(f(ϕ+Ur)−f(Ur))dx+∫∞−∞(∂tϕ−∂x2ϕ)F(Ur)dx.\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\frac{\beta+1}{2}\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\frac{\gamma+1}{2}\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\\ &+\|\,\partial_{t}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\alpha\,\|\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\beta\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\gamma\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{3}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\\ &=-\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\big(\,\partial_{t}\phi-\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\big)\,\bigl(\,f(\phi+U^{r})-f(U^{r})\,\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &+\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\big(\,\partial_{t}\phi-\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\big)\,F(U^{r})\,\mathrm{d}x.\end{aligned} (4.4)

By using the Young inequality, we estimate the each terms on the right-hand side of (4.4) as follows.

|∫−∞∞(∂tϕ−∂x2ϕ)​(f⁡(ϕ+Ur)−f⁡(Ur))​dx|≤ϵ⁡(‖∂tϕ‖L22+‖∂x2ϕ‖L22)+Cϵ,β​‖f⁡(ϕ+Ur)−f⁡(Ur)‖L22,\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\left|\,\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\big(\,\partial_{t}\phi-\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\big)\,\bigl(\,f(\phi+U^{r})-f(U^{r})\,\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\right|\\ &\leq\epsilon\left(\,\|\,\partial_{t}\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\right)+C_{\epsilon,\beta}\,\left\|\,f(\phi+U^{r})-f(U^{r})\,\right\|_{L^{2}}^{2},\end{aligned} (4.5)
|∫−∞∞(∂tϕ−∂x2ϕ)​F​(Ur)​dx|≤ϵ⁡(‖∂tϕ‖L22+‖∂x2ϕ‖L22)+Cϵ,β​‖F⁡(Ur)‖L22,\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\left|\,\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\big(\,\partial_{t}\phi-\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\big)\,F(U^{r})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\right|\\ &\leq\epsilon\left(\,\|\,\partial_{t}\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\,\right)+C_{\epsilon,\beta}\,\left\|\,F(U^{r})\,\right\|_{L^{2}}^{2},\end{aligned} (4.6)

for ϵ>0\epsilon>0. Choosing ϵ\epsilon suitably small, substituting (4.5) and (4.6) into (4.4), and using Lemma 4.3, we obtain the desired estimate.

Thus, we complete the proof of Proposition 4.4.

Remark 4.5. Similarly to Lemma 4.2, we have the uniform boundedness of ∂xϕ\partial_{x}\phi by using Proposition 4.4 that

supt∈[0,T],x∈ℝ|∂xϕ⁡(t,x)|≤Cϕ0.\sup_{t\in[0,T],\,x\in\mathbb{R}}\,|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t,x)\,|\leq C_{\phi_{0}}.

We further show the a priori estimate for ∂x2ϕ\partial_{x}^{2}\phi and ∂x3ϕ\partial_{x}^{3}\phi as follows.

Proposition 4.6. There exists a positive constant Cϕ0C_{\phi_{0}} such that

‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖H12+∫0t(‖∂t∂xϕ⁡(τ)‖H12+‖∂x3ϕ⁡(τ)‖H12)​𝑑τ≤Cϕ0(t∈[ 0,T]).\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\int^{t}_{0}\left(\,\|\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}\phi(\tau)\,\|_{H^{1}}^{2}+\|\,\partial_{x}^{3}\phi(\tau)\,\|_{H^{1}}^{2}\,\right)\,\mathrm{d}\tau\leq C_{\phi_{0}}\quad\big(\,t\in[\,0,\,T\,]\,\big).

Proof of Proposition 4.6. Multiplying the equation in (3.2) by ∂x4ϕ−∂t∂x2ϕ\partial_{x}^{4}\phi-\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi and integrating it with respect to xx, we have, after integration by parts, that

β+12​dd​t​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22+α+γ2​dd​t​‖∂x3ϕ⁡(t)‖L22+‖∂t∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L22+α​‖∂t∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L22+β​‖∂x3ϕ⁡(t)‖L22+γ​‖∂x4ϕ⁡(t)‖L22=−∫∞−∞(∂x4ϕ−∂t∂x2ϕ)(f(ϕ+Ur)−f(Ur))dx+∫∞−∞(∂x4ϕ−∂t∂x2ϕ)F(Ur)dx.\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\frac{\beta+1}{2}\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2}\,\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{3}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\\ &+\|\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\alpha\,\|\,\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\beta\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{3}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}+\gamma\,\|\,\partial_{x}^{4}\phi(t)\,\|_{L^{2}}^{2}\\ &=-\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\big(\,\partial_{x}^{4}\phi-\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\big)\,\bigl(\,f(\phi+U^{r})-f(U^{r})\,\bigr)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &+\int^{\infty}_{-\infty}\big(\,\partial_{x}^{4}\phi-\partial_{t}\partial_{x}^{2}\phi\,\big)\,F(U^{r})\,\mathrm{d}x.\end{aligned} (4.7)

The each terms on the right-hand side of (4.7) can be estimated quite similarly to (4.5) and (4.6). Therefore, we obtain the desired estimate by using Lemma 4.3.

Thus, we complete the proof of Proposition 4.6.

Remark 4.7. Similarly to Lemma 4.2 and remark 4.5, we have the uniform boundedness of ∂x2ϕ\partial_{x}^{2}\phi by using Proposition 4.6 that

supt∈[0,T],x∈ℝ|∂x2ϕ⁡(t,x)|≤Cϕ0.\sup_{t\in[0,T],\,x\in\mathbb{R}}\,|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t,x)\,|\leq C_{\phi_{0}}.

5 Remarks on the uniform estimates

It is worthwhile to mention the uniform estimates of the solution ϕ\phi to (3.2). By using the Sobolev inequality to ϕ\phi, ∂xϕ\partial_{x}\phi, ∂x2ϕ\partial_{x}^{2}\phi, ∂x3ϕ\partial_{x}^{3}\phi, ∂x3ϕ\partial_{x}^{3}\phi, ∂tϕ\partial_{t}\phi and ∂t∂xϕ\partial_{t}\partial_{x}\phi, and integration by parts, we obtain

supx∈ℝ|ϕ⁡(t,x)|≤2​‖ϕ⁡(t)‖L212​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L212≤min⁡{2​‖ϕ⁡(t)‖L234​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L214,‖ϕ⁡(t)‖H1}≤2​‖ϕ⁡(t)‖L234​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L218​‖∂x3ϕ⁡(t)‖L218≤2​‖ϕ⁡(t)‖L234​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L218​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L2116​‖∂x4ϕ⁡(t)‖L2116,\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\phi(t,x)\,|&\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\\ &\leq\min\left\{\,\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{3}{4}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{4}}_{L^{2}},\,\|\,\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{1}}\,\right\}\\ &\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{3}{4}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{8}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{3}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{8}}_{L^{2}}\\ &\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{3}{4}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{8}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{16}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{4}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{16}}_{L^{2}},\end{aligned} (5.1)
supx∈ℝ|∂xϕ⁡(t,x)|≤2​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L212​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L212≤min⁡{2​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L234​‖∂x3ϕ⁡(t)‖L214,‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖H1}≤2​‖∂xϕ⁡(t)‖L234​‖∂x2ϕ⁡(t)‖L218​‖∂x4ϕ⁡(t)‖L218,\displaystyle\begin{aligned} \sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t,x)\,|&\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{2}}_{L^{2}}\\ &\leq\min\left\{\,\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{3}{4}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{3}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{4}}_{L^{2}},\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|_{H^{1}}\,\right\}\\ &\leq\sqrt{2}\,\|\,\partial_{x}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{3}{4}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{2}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{8}}_{L^{2}}\|\,\partial_{x}^{4}\phi(t)\,\|^{\frac{1}{8}}_{L^{2}},\end{aligned} (5.2)
